title: Afterhours infra bullet journal
content:
2026-03-12 — afterhours quick log

Top-of-shift mental checklist:
- Check pool headroom (pools: infer-prod-a, infer-prod-b) — target spare GPUs >= 3
- Verify NIC flaps resolved in us-west-2-rack-7 (alerts came 01:12AM) — asked SRE to watch for CRC errors
- Confirm storage IOPS on checkpoint mounts (nfs-cp01) not throttling long SGX runs

Morning tasks (do first on wake):
1) Drain one GPU from infer-prod-b for kernel upgrade (no traffic policy: canary fallback to variant: small-quant)
   - kubectl cordon node gpu-node-17 && kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
   - notify #infra-ops, post ETA 30m
2) Bump autoscaler target for low-latency queue to 6 -> observe 15m metrics
3) Revisit p99 latency alert thresholds after last deploy (PR 998)

Notes to self / quick findings:
- Observed two long-running jobs hogging 12GB each on a 24GB card; add soft-limits for user:ai-loadtest account
- KV cache growth pattern: steady for first 512 tokens, then jump at 1024 token boundary -> look into shard placement for attention cache
- Coredump from modelserv-3 shows BLAS mismatch; maybe incompatible MKL linked in nightly container build (tag: nightly-2026-03-09)

Tickets / follow-ups:
- RW-4321: capacity bump request from search-team (waiting on finance sign-off). Action: prepare usage projection table (tokens vs GPUs) and drop into ticket by EOD
- Open PR: platform#998 needs a small update to env var REDWOOD_BATCH_MAX=64 to match new kernel. Add note to release train

Commands I used / will reuse:
- top-of-day health: curl -s http://console.internal/api/pools/infer-prod-a | jq '.available_gpus'
- reclaim idle: python tools/reclaim_idle.py --age=15m --dry-run
- quick NIC check: ethtool -S eth0 | grep tx_errors

Parking lot / ideas:
- Lightweight tracer for KV cache churn (small binary instrumented into runtime) — low-risk canary for dedicated pool
- Auto-tiering: if job queue size > 500 and avg latency > 400ms then trigger quantized-model fallback for non-critical routes

Questions to answer next shift:
- Did draining gpu-node-17 cause any fallback cascade? Check model variant fallback logs
- Are we comfortable setting soft-limit to 10GB for ai-loadtest? Quick AB test tomorrow with one job

Random reminders:
- Ping finance about reserved capacity proposal before Friday
- Bring up follow-on meeting with console team about per-route cost breakdowns (copy of slides in drive/contrib/cost-breakdowns)

End-of-shift quick status (leave short):
- drain started at 03:40AM, node reboots clean, no job evictions beyond expected (one retry), pool spare GPUs now 4
- logged RW-4321 projection snippet in comments

---
Tiny personal note: stop relying on single terminal for critical commands; use screen/tmux and upload logs to /tmp/ops-dump before rebooting nodes.
